name: noctalia-ipc
description: The shell IPC verbs this project sends, with the arguments each one takes and the line of the pinned release each was read from. data/design/noctalia.json records the configuration keys the shell has; this record is the other half of the same surface -- the commands that read and write them while the session is running -- and the settings application may not send a verb that is not listed here.
_note: Kept apart from noctalia.json because the two answer different questions and are verified differently: a config key is a field in a schema struct, a verb is an entry in the command table, and a key can exist with no verb that reaches it (Do Not Disturb is exactly that case -- IPC only, no key at all in v5.4.1). One trap this record exists to prevent: the command table's header also declares positional-argument names and choice values as string literals, so extracting every quoted string from src/cli/schema_msg.h yields 204 names of which only some are commands. `monitor-selector` is the clearest example -- it is a positional several bar commands accept, not a verb, and sending it would be refused at runtime rather than caught here. Every entry below was matched against an `inline constexpr Command` definition.

verified_against.reply_note: The handler prints one line and exits non-zero when it refuses. iarch/lib/modes.py reads the reply text rather than trusting the exit code, because a handler that answers 'ok' as a no-op -- caffeine already in that state, src/idle/idle_inhibitor.cpp:175-212 -- and a handler that could not be reached are different facts and only the text tells them apart.

source: noctalia-dev/noctalia at v5.4.1: src/cli/schema_msg.h (the Command table, its Positional declarations and its choice lists), src/app/application_ipc.cpp:158-159 (what a handler prints for Do Not Disturb) and src/idle/idle_inhibitor.cpp:175-212 (what caffeine answers, including the no-op ok)

arguments.name: path
arguments.note: Dotted config path, for example theme.shell_mode. The path is checked against data/design/noctalia.json before it is sent, so a typo is refused here rather than answered with an unknown-setting warning.

used_by: iarch/settings-app: the Bar, Dock & Panels, Features, Power & Idle and Appearance pages read what the shell runs before showing it

arguments.name: value
arguments.note: A TOML value, and the header's own example is explicit that a string is quoted: "'light'". So a boolean goes as true, a number as 900, a float as 0.5 and a string as 'light' -- sending light unquoted is a parse failure in the shell, not a silent default.

not_commands.what_it_really_is: A positional-argument name that six bar commands accept, not a verb
not_commands.why_it_matters: It appears in the header's string literals alongside real verbs, so a list extracted by grepping quoted strings includes it. Sending `noctalia msg monitor-selector` would be refused by the shell's own verb lookup, and only at runtime.

not_commands.spelling: bar-name, connector, target, step, path, value, mode, kind, profile, state, level, direction
not_commands.what_it_really_is: Positional-argument names and choice values, not verbs
not_commands.why_it_matters: Same trap as monitor-selector: 204 quoted strings in this header, of which the Commands are a subset.

not_used.why: This application offers Lock now and Suspend and stops there. A control panel that can end a session, reboot or power off the machine turns one mis-click into lost work, and the shell's own session menu already draws those actions with the confirmation the shell owns.
not_used.evidence: src/cli/schema_msg.h:79-80 lists the seven actions; SECURITY.md's rule that a diagnostic or a panel never takes an action it was not asked for

not_used.why: Syncing the login screen needs the polkit action org.noctalia.greeter.sync-appearance and a state directory owned by root, which is why Part 3 recorded the whole greeter surface and emitted nothing. A settings row that prompts for administrative authentication to change a screen the user is not looking at is not a feature this project ships.
not_used.evidence: src/cli/schema_msg.h:530 and data/design/greeter.json (auto_sync and privilege_command are withheld)

not_used.why: Despite the name, this is an audio effects profile (its kind choices are output and input), not a glass effect profile. Recorded because the name invites exactly the wrong mapping from this project's own `preset` and `effects` switches.
